title: Denmark CPR register breach, Nov 2026

subject.name: CPR
subject.about: The CPR (Det Centrale Personregister) is Denmark's central register of people, run by the CPR administration within the Ministry of Research, Education and Digitalisation. It is the central supplier of basic personal details, such as names and addresses, to public authorities and private companies.

disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by the Danish government, the CPR administration, any news outlet, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: The CPR is Denmark's national register of people. The November incident reached about 11,000 people's CPR numbers, names and addresses; the separate October incident reached about 8.8 million.
who_is_affected: About 11,000 people whose CPR numbers, names and addresses were looked up. The ministry has not said how they will be told. It advises everyone never to give out a password on a call or email, even to someone who knows their name, address and CPR number.

known.text: Denmark's ministry says unauthorised people got the CPR numbers, names and addresses of about 11,000 people.
The access came through suspicious lookups in the register from a company, noticed on Monday Nov 23.
New monitoring of lookups, brought in after October's breach, stopped it.
The police are investigating both the October and November incidents.

not_known.text: Which company the lookups came from, and whether it is the one involved in October.
What the security review of the CPR system will find.
